findings.title: Hardcoded Default Secret Key Fallback in JWT Verification
findings.data_type: SYNTHETIC / DEMONSTRATION DATA - NOT VERIFIED WORLD MONITOR VULNERABILITIES
findings.description: The JWT verification module falls back to a hardcoded string if the environment variable JWT_SECRET is not defined. Attackers can forge administrative tokens using the hardcoded default key.
findings.remediation: Remove the hardcoded fallback secret. Ensure server initialization aborts if JWT_SECRET is missing or under 256 bits of entropy.

findings.title: Missing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) on Telemetry Export API
findings.evidence: router.get('/api/v1/telemetry/export', authenticateToken, (req, res) => { /* exports full DB dump */ });
findings.description: The endpoint checks for a valid authentication token but fails to verify if the authenticated user has administrative privileges, allowing standard users to dump system telemetry.
findings.remediation: Attach an authorization middleware (e.g., `requireRole('admin')`) to the route handler before returning data.

findings.title: Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Wildcard Header
findings.description: Wildcard CORS origin combined with credentials allows any third-party website to initiate authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of legitimate users.
findings.remediation: Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to an explicit whitelist of trusted domains and disallow wildcard origins when credentials are allowed.

findings.title: Verbose Debug Error Messages Leaking Stack Traces to Client
findings.evidence: res.status(500).json({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack, internalContext: err.config });
findings.description: Unhandled server errors leak internal stack traces, system paths, and database query details to HTTP response bodies in production.
findings.remediation: Sanitize HTTP 500 error responses in production environments. Log detailed stack traces internally to secure logger instances only.

findings.title: Unbound Dynamic Database Query Parameter in Log Search API
findings.description: Constructing dynamic MongoDB query code directly from user input allows arbitrary JavaScript code execution in the database engine context.
findings.remediation: Replace dynamic `$where` evaluation with structured parameter queries or parameterized regular expressions.

attackPaths.name: Full Authentication Bypass to Unrestricted Data Exfiltration
attackPaths.description: An actor leverages default JWT secrets (SEC-001) to forge administrative tokens, bypasses unverified API role checks (SEC-002), and extracts system stack traces & telemetry (SEC-004).
attackPaths.impact: Complete compromise of backend API authorization boundary and sensitive telemetry exposure.

attackPaths.name: Cross-Origin Remote Injection & Database Execution Path
attackPaths.description: A malicious cross-origin site triggers cross-domain requests due to wildcard CORS (SEC-003) into the dynamic log search API (SEC-005), enabling remote database injection.
attackPaths.impact: Unauthorized client-side cross-site request execution leading to backend query execution.

attackPaths.name: Cross-Origin Token Forgery & Access Control Escalation
attackPaths.description: An attacker leverages permissive CORS headers (SEC-003) to issue cross-site requests, uses the default hardcoded JWT secret (SEC-001) to construct admin tokens, and accesses privileged endpoints lacking role checks (SEC-002).
attackPaths.impact: Unrestricted administrative escalation originating from cross-domain web browser contexts.

attackPaths.name: Reconnaissance-Driven Dynamic Query Injection
attackPaths.description: Detailed error messages and stack traces leaked via debug endpoints (SEC-004) reveal internal data schemas, enabling targeted unescaped parameter injection into the log search API (SEC-005).
attackPaths.impact: Targeted database query injection facilitated by internal stack trace leaks.
